I am 65 years old, no schooling, been on this 6 mu for 45 years. I do what works. My old way gives me about 450 kg wheat per mu and 550 kg maize. Same as last year, same as the year before. Why change?

For wheat, I plant in October after the maize is off. I buy the improved seed from the village dealer — everyone buys there, the seed is fine. Before planting I run the rotary tiller through once, then broadcast my base fertilizer. I put down one bag of compound — that 15-15-15 kind, about 50 jin per mu — when I sow. After winter when the wheat greens up, I top-dress with urea, half a bag per mu, maybe a touch more if the leaves look pale. I water from my well four times: once before the cold, once at green-up, once at jointing when the stem stretches, and once when the head is filling. I spray twice — once for the weeds in spring, once for aphids before harvest.

For maize, I drill right into the wheat stubble in June, no ploughing, just open the row and drop the seed. Hybrid seed only — the old kinds give nothing, every neighbor uses hybrid. I put compound down with the seed, about one bag per mu, then top-dress urea when the maize is knee-high. Summer rain usually does the watering, but if July stays dry I run the well once or twice. I spray once for armyworm and once for the weeds early on.

Fertilizer is the biggest expense after seed. I would rather put a little extra than come up short — a thin harvest hurts more than a few extra yuan on urea. My neighbors do about the same. With one person in the house and 6 mu, I do not hire much help, only at wheat harvest when the combine comes through the village.
